results.summary_before: This design is an 8-bit binary counter built from eight chained D flip-flops that increment on the clock input and present the count on the eight outputs. It is created as part of a workshop and uses the Wokwi simulator. The design is intended for educational purposes, demonstrating sequential logic. The pin names map the outputs to 7-segment display segments, but no function is described.
results.summary: This design sends the string 'Hello\n' over UART using a shift register with hardcoded initial values loaded into a looped feedback path. It also fills remaining die space with an 'RNN' module made from flip-flops feeding into each other, driven by inputs 0-3 and producing outputs 0-3. To test UART, connect the UART output to a microcontroller or scope, set load/enable low then high, set output enable high, and observe the string. The design has been silicon-tested and reported working by a tester who connected it to a serial port and saw it print Hello.
